It includes research training after the clinical year; research years do not themselves constitute an additional specialty or board. The institution lists pediatric Hematology/Oncology separately; it is outside this adult packet and pediatric board/curriculum is distinct.
boardEligibilityNotice: No completion of this independent self-study course confers eligibility. ABIM certification ordinarily requires prior ABIM Internal Medicine certification, requisite qualifying accredited fellowship training, documented clinical competence, unrestricted license, and passing the relevant subspecialty examination. ABIM policies and eligibility can change; candidates must confirm current rules with ABIM. Dual hematology/medical oncology certification has its own combined training and clinical-time requirements; do not infer eligibility from track names.

boardStatus.specialtyExam: No separate thoracic oncology certification board or thoracic oncology board examination identified in ABIM’s published certification roster/policy as checked 2026-10-07. The specialty name denotes an institutional clinical/research fellowship focus, not a distinct board-certified subspecialty.
boardStatus.relatedExams: ABIM offers Medical Oncology certification and separately Hematology certification. Board examination eligibility is governed by ABIM policy and depends on prior internal medicine certification, qualifying accredited training, licensure and competency requirements; the Dana-Farber advanced fellowship alone is not a substitute for that training.

boardEligibilityNotice: Independent course completion confers no ABIM eligibility. Dana-Farber’s public page states that applicants must have completed medical oncology training (minimum two years) or hematology/oncology (minimum three years), and must be eligible for a limited or permanent Massachusetts medical license; it also gives licensing-examination qualifications and other conditions. These are institutional applicant requirements, not a guarantee of appointment, medical license, ABIM eligibility, or certification. ABIM’s published policy requires qualifying accredited U.S./Canadian subspecialty fellowship training for certification. Confirm current terms with Dana-Farber, the relevant licensing authority and ABIM.
